transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Ever since my daughter left for basic training, I just... I come home and the house feels dead. I can’t seem to keep myself together. I’ve been crying in my truck before shifts, and at work I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. I’ve been snapping at the younger guys too. I don’t go out on the water anymore or work on my sculpture. I just don’t see the point.
Did these feelings start after your daughter left for basic training?
Yeah. I was managing okay before she shipped out. Then within a few weeks of her leaving for basic training, everything started feeling like this.
Since your daughter left, have you felt down or depressed most days?
Yeah, most days. I get home and the house just feels dead, and I don’t really see the point in doing the things I used to enjoy.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of killing yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean. I know I’ve been feeling really low, but I haven’t really thought about that.
How long have you been feeling this down nearly every day?
It’s been about a month now—since she left. I’ve been feeling down pretty much every day since then.
Since your daughter left, have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah. I’ve been missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. It’s like I can’t keep my mind on what I’m doing.
Since your daughter left, have you been feeling especially nervous or on edge?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve been feeling low, but I haven’t noticed being especially nervous or on edge.
Since your daughter left, have you had trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular trouble with sleep.
Have these feelings been interfering with your ability to do your job?
Yeah. My supervisor took me off a more complex welding job because I wasn’t coordinating safely enough. And I missed the deadline for a sculpture submission—I just never got it finished.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any change in your appetite?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t paid much attention to my appetite lately.
Since your daughter left, have you felt noticeably slowed down in your movements or speech?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed my movements or speech being slower.
Since your daughter left, have you been feeling worthless or overly guilty?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling that way specifically.
Since your daughter left, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed being unusually tired or low on energy.
Before your daughter left, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time before this when I felt depressed like that for days or weeks.
Since your daughter left, have you lost interest or pleasure in most things you usually enjoy?
Yeah. I used to go out on the water and work on my sculpture, but since she left, I just... I don’t see the point in any of it.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you would expect for your daughter leaving for basic training?

Yeah, I think so. I knew I’d miss her, but I didn’t expect to feel like I come home to a dead house and just can’t hold myself together. I’m crying in my truck before shifts, messing up welding steps I’ve done for years, snapping at the younger guys. It’s more than I thought it would be.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?
I... I’m not sure what you mean by that. I just know I’ve been feeling really overwhelmed.
Have you found yourself wishing you would not wake up?
I’m not sure. I just feel overwhelmed a lot, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself?
No... I haven’t had thoughts of killing myself. I’ve just been feeling really overwhelmed.
Since your daughter left, have you been eating noticeably less than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to how much I’ve been eating.
